front: Why is Telegram Custom built on stock upstream rather than forking AyuGram?
back: AyuGram is a reference to read, not a base - its diff would be someone else's to rebase through and trust. Base is stock telegramdesktop/tdesktop and DrKLO/Telegram.

front: Why was 64Gram dropped as a candidate base (2026-09-23)?
back: One maintainer, feature list frozen since 2024-08.

front: What's the patch philosophy for Telegram Custom?
back: Surgical patches - each feature is one small patch, no reformatting, no renames that upstream would conflict with.

front: What system libs does the Telegram Custom desktop build link against?
back: Manjaro stable's system libs, pinned to the version Manjaro stable packages (Arch PKGBUILD recipe) - either in a manjarolinux/base GitHub Actions container, or locally with the same script.

front: Where does Telegram Custom (desktop) install to, and where's its data?
back: App: ~/.local/opt/telegram-custom (previous build kept as .prev for rollback). Data: ~/.local/share/TelegramCustom, separate from the official client (needs its own login). Pacman's telegram-desktop stays as fallback.

front: Why do Telegram Custom's source/build trees live in ~/.cache/telegram-custom instead of under the project folder?
back: The space in "AI Projects" breaks gobject-introspection's libtool step.

front: Telegram Custom: what stays stock vs customized visually?
back: Stories and similar channels stay visible; themes stay stock. Purple is only the logo (generated at build time), showing because the app runs under its own id org.telegram.desktop.custom.

front: Why is the Telegram Custom repo public?
back: For unlimited GitHub Actions minutes; secrets must never be committed.

front: Where does Telegram Custom's Android build happen, and why?
back: GitHub Actions only, arm64 only, package org.telegram.messenger.custom - minutes are free for a public repo and no local toolchain is wanted.

front: What does every push to main do in Telegram Custom's CI?
back: Publishes a GitHub Release (both desktop and Android workflows); branch builds stay as artifacts only.

front: When does a Telegram Custom feature branch merge to main?
back: Only once it's been tried on the device - main is what CI builds and publishes.

front: Where do Telegram Custom's signing key and passwords live?
back: .secrets/ (gitignored), with copies in GitHub repo secrets; api_id lives in .env.
context: Back up .secrets/: losing the signing key means every update needs an uninstall on the phone.

front: Install the newest CI desktop build of Telegram Custom?
back: desktop/install.sh --from-ci (needs Manjaro stable up to date - the build links against current stable libs).

front: A Telegram Custom desktop build is broken. How to go back?
back: desktop/install.sh --rollback swaps the previous build (.prev) back in.

front: How to update Telegram Custom desktop to a newer tdesktop upstream version?
back: Edit desktop/UPSTREAM (version + the two hashes from the Arch PKGBUILD at that tag), then rerun desktop/build.sh.

front: How to update Telegram Custom Android to a newer DrKLO/Telegram commit?
back: Paste the newest "update to X" commit sha from DrKLO/Telegram into line 1 of android/UPSTREAM, push.

front: How to write a new desktop patch for Telegram Custom?
back: Edit inside ~/.cache/telegram-custom/src/tdesktop-<ver>-full (branch custom = upstream + patches), commit, then git format-patch against upstream into desktop/patches. build.sh resets and re-applies the whole series, so the patch files are the truth.

front: Hide a gallery folder (e.g. Screenshots) from "All media" on Telegram Custom Android?
back: Attach -> tap the album name at top -> long-press the folder. It stays listed marked "hidden"; long-press again to undo.

front: What does "Send and move to trash" do on Telegram Custom Android?
back: After photos finish uploading, Android asks once to move the originals to its trash; nothing is touched if any send fails. Android 11+.

front: Spy essentials (deleted/edited message log) on Telegram Custom - plaintext or encrypted?
back: Pick: encrypted under the local passcode (AyuGram keeps them in plaintext).
